subject: Refine: prioritization options for Q2 org structure
body:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Momentum Strategy - Kara Patel <kara.patel@momentum.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Refine: prioritization options for Q2 org structure

Team —

Attached is the first pass of the prioritization memo I promised for QBR prep. Two quick things up front: I want this to be concise for the exec readout and pragmatic for the first 60 days of execution. Please focus comments on clear trade-offs and operational risk.

Attachments: prioritization_memo_v1.pdf (5 pages) — executive summary + options, org_structure_option_charts.xlsx (2 sheets) — headcount and reporting diagrams. Also a working copy is at: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/prioritization-memo-v1

High level summary (three options):

Option A — Consolidate by function (Engineering / Platform / Product).
- Simpler reporting lines, faster cross-functional prioritization.
- Risk: loss of product-domain expertise; potential disruptions for platform commitments.

Option B — Hybrid squad model with shared platform core and vertical product pods (recommended baseline).
- Keeps domain expertise while reducing duplicate infra work by centralizing platform services.
- Allows targeted reassignments and pilot of 3 cross-domain product pods in Q2.
- Risk: requires clear SLAs between platform and pods; initial coordination overhead.

Option C — Minimal structural changes + programmatic prioritization (no reporting changes).
- Low disruption; quick to implement via PM/eng prioritization cadence.
- Risk: continues current inefficiencies; harder to scale predictable delivery and cost-savings targets.

Asks:
- Please add inline comments in the Drive doc or reply here with explicit redlines by EOD Monday, Jan 22.
- Jonas: can you validate the platform SLA draft in sheet 2 of the workbook?
- Lauren: recommend who should own the QBR slide and who will field questions.
- Neha & Rishi: highlight any regulatory/personnel constraints we need to call out for private deployments.

I want to present a refined recommendation to the execs during the QBR planning session (Thursday, Jan 28). If we converge on an approach, we'll prepare a one-slide decision + a two-week rollout checklist for comms.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
VP, People & Strategy
Redwood Inference

---

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Jan 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Refine: prioritization options for Q2 org structure

On Fri, Jan 20, 2028 at 9:12 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Attached is the first pass of the prioritization memo I promised for QBR prep. Two quick things up front: I want this to be concise for the exec readout and pragmatic for the first 60 days of execution. Please focus comments on clear trade-offs and operational risk.
> 
> High level summary (three options):
> 
> Option B — Hybrid squad model with shared platform core and vertical product pods (recommended baseline).

Thanks for pulling this together — good framing. A few inline notes from me (refer to sheet 1 comments):
- Option B makes the most sense for delivery velocity and cost-savings, I agree. Suggest we explicitly call out a pilot measurement: throughput (stories/week), mean time to resolve infra defects, and infra $/token impact.
- On centralizing platform: we must preserve a fast path for urgent product-side experiments. Propose a "fast-track" SLA: 24–48 hour triage for low-latency experiments. Without it, pods will keep shipping shadow infra.
- Headcount table: the assumptions on tempo (hiring vs reallocation) are optimistic. If hiring lags, we need a contingency plan to delay one pod pilot rather than scale across three simultaneously.

I also added a suggested slide layout for the QBR slide (sheet 3 in the workbook). Happy to take the owner role for the platform SLA section.

Jonas
SVP, Serving & Runtime

---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jan 2028 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Refine: prioritization options for Q2 org structure

+1 to Option B with the modifications Jonas suggested.

Quick edit suggestion for the memo: under "communication cadence" call out a single point of contact for exec escalations (recommend: Rishi for infra/ops escalations, Neha for compliance/regulatory questions).

I'll own the QBR slide deck and coordinate a dry run on Monday, Jan 26 at 10:00am PT — can everyone make that window? I plan to build a single decision slide + three bullets of operational ask.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Product Experience

---

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Momentum Strategy - Kara Patel <kara.patel@momentum.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jan 2028 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Refine: prioritization options for Q2 org structure — decision path

Thanks all for the quick reads and the constructive comments. Summary and decisions: 

1) Direction: move forward with Option B (Hybrid squad model) with two changes — (a) start with two product pods and keep the third as contingent based on hiring velocity; (b) formalize a "fast-track" platform SLA for experiments (24–48 hour triage) to avoid shadow infra.

2) Owners & next steps: 
- Platform SLA & metrics (throughput / MTTR / infra $/token): Jonas (owner); deliverable: SLA + measurement dashboard by Feb 9.
- QBR slide + exec dry run: Lauren (owner); dry run: Mon, Jan 26 at 10:00am PT.
- Compliance/regulatory call-outs for private deployments: Neha (owner); flag any constraints by end of next week (Feb 2).
- Escalation point for infra ops: Rishi (owner).

3) Communication plan: Vanessa & Kara will draft a short all-hands comm and an email to impacted teams. Draft comms will be ready for review by Jan 30; plan to announce at the Feb 6 all-hands.

4) Deliverables attached: updated prioritization_memo_v1.pdf (reflects the decision path) and the org_structure_option_charts.xlsx with the updated pilot plan. Please confirm you have access to the Drive copy and add final comments there rather than replying with large attachments.

If no major redlines by EOD Friday, Jan 27 we will lock the slide and the comms deck. Appreciate the quick turn here — this gives us a clean narrative for QBR and a pragmatic rollout cadence.

-Vanessa
VP, People & Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: prioritization_memo_v1.pdf (updated), org_structure_option_charts.xlsx (updated)
